strategy.summary: Reproduce the evalf_log precision bug in SymPy by running the PR's test_issue_28280 on the buggy commit 3e18ad01a1e4 (expected to fail, since x > 20 evaluates False) and on the fixed revision (expected to pass). Pure Python, no compiled extensions, so an editable install from the checked-out tree is sufficient.

pinned_because: sympy version unpinned: no documented constraint in the evidence, so the checked-out revision itself defines the version under test; mpmath is required by sympy and left unpinned because no era constraint is stated

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 3e18ad01a1e4 the test fails: the assertion x > 20 for x = 20 + log(1 + S(10)**-10) evaluates False, so pytest reports an AssertionError. On the fixed revision (the PR head with the evalf_log change) the same test passes, with both x > 20 and y > 20 True. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.
risks: The buggy-side failure is specific to the evalf_log code path at the default precision; if the environment's sympy is an installed release rather than the checked-out tree, the test will not reproduce. Use the editable install from the repository so the buggy source is what runs.
The PR's printed value 9.99999999950000E-11 is the author's output, not a verified oracle; the test asserts only the boolean comparison, so the transition does not depend on it.

Issue #28514 (strict=True precision error on log(y/z)) is a related but separate report; the test_issue_28280 transition does not exercise strict mode, and the passages do not reconcile the two identifiers, so do not treat #28514 as the oracle.
xre_acc being None is an open question in the discussion; the test does not depend on how None is handled, but a differing fix could change the outcome on other inputs.
No platform or compiler dependence is evidenced: the behaviour is pure-Python mpmath/evalf arithmetic, so it should transition on any architecture. No sanitiser or threading condition is stated.
Python version is not stated in the evidence (python_version null); any Python 3 supported by the checked-out sympy should work, but this is not verified.

oracle.why: The test asserts a boolean comparison x > 20, which is an exact check with no numerical tolerance needed.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 3e18ad01a1e4 the assertion `assert x > 20` sees False, because evalf at default precision rounds log(1+1e-10) to 0, so x evaluates to exactly 20 and the strict comparison fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision evalf_log computes the argument minus one accurately and restores precision, so x > 20 and y > 20 both evaluate True and the test passes.
